First-person present form explained; independent use pending.

Introduced in te autorizo; direct/indirect-object distinctions have not yet been taught.
Introduced by breaking publicarlo into publicar + lo; gender distinctions not yet taught.
Shown in Reviso el documento; independent recall pending.
Used in an example of a full noun object after a verb.
Spontaneous acknowledgement; no claim of durable mastery.

Earlier why-question spacing corrected. In four explanation requests in session10, correctly used two words por que for intended why, with accented qué supplied. Clause meaning/formation correct; orthography separate.
Correctly used in a spontaneous question. No separate gender or article lesson was given.
Initially separated as revisar lo; then used correctly in Queremos revisarlo. Recall after a gap remains untested.
Used spontaneously in a grammatical question.
Wrote possibilidad; supplied the spelling posibilidad with one s.

Used in Queremos probarla after a reminder of probar.

De omitted in both Hablo un poco español and Queremos aprender un poco español on 10 November. Then correctly selected de in a gap and retained it in Comprendemos un poco de español. Immediate transfer distinguished from recall.
Supplied as the natural spelling after pocetito. General diminutive formation not yet taught.
Supplied in más bien un poquitito as a natural reformulation; independent use untested.
Used para + infinitive after a model and selected it correctly in a cued choice.
Learner supplied this verb, then reused it in a modelled purpose sentence.
Wrote conversationes twice; supplied conversaciones. Independent correct spelling not observed.
Supplied ñ and capitalization in the country name; recorded as vocabulary, not a personal circumstance.
Supplied correctly in a self-created sentence and later recall.
Tutor supplied obtener información; learner then reused obtener after the model.
Meaning clear; accent in información supplied. Keyboard limitations remain unassessed.
Correct prompted use after the form was shown.
Correct form after introduction; the same sentence needed a querer correction.
Correct immediate response after an explicit earlier model and stem-preservation explanation.

Correct full stem in Comprendemos un poco de español, then correctly used comprendemos with porque leemos in the next client-date reply. Exact elapsed interval unknown; longer-term retention untested.
Correct question word and word order; supplied accent and punctuation. Keyboard constraints remain unassessed.
Correctly used after introduction; one following verb/object needed correction, then Necesitamos publicarlo was complete.
Correct verb form throughout practice; object or negation initially missing in some responses, followed by correct No lo podemos publicar.
Supplied correctly in a real Spanish work request.
Used in a work request and readiness question; noun is masculine.
Supplied correctly in the logo request.
Introduced with the actual logo and correctly used with attached pronouns.
Correctly used for el logo after a model.
Correctly selected for the stated referent la función.
After the session11 masculine-adjective error with función, correctly used feminine lista in four session12 readiness contexts. Recheck after a longer gap.
After earlier errors, correctly recalled La función todavía no está lista in session12 after intervening exchanges; reused in a contrasting sentence. Delayed retention untested.
Correctly used before está and at the end of Podemos usarla ya; other senses not taught.
Spontaneous Yo No se was natural in meaning; sé accent and capitalization supplied. No sé modelled as the usual shorter alternative. No general saber conjugation lesson given.
Introduced as a connector, then correctly used in two prompted contrasts during the same round. Delayed recall untested.

vocabulary.english: this (before a feminine singular noun in the practised phrase)
vocabulary.note: After repeated esto función errors, correctly produced full Crea esta función without a fresh model, then retained esta función in the test command; exact long-term retention untested.
Correct command after revisar → revisa explanation; noun-reference errors assessed separately.
Correctly used after crear → crea model; delayed recall untested.
Correct informal Lee esta función with tú explicit, then léela after an earlier model, accent supplied. Earlier formal lea was valid; independent register switching untested.
Used in five prompted commands after phrase model; no independent long-gap recall established.
Following earlier proba errors, correctly recalled Prueba esta función without a fresh stem hint in session04 and used pruébala with accent supplied. Same-day recall; longer-term retention untested.
Produced grammatical Lea esto por favor when sequence expected informal tú. Formal meaning acknowledged and tú lee modelled. Intentional register choice and retention unassessed.
Initial infinitive revisarla was corrected to revísala. Later correctly formed revisala during positive/negative contrast, with written accent supplied.
Correct command form and lo in Revisalo after feminine model; written accent supplied.
Correct command base with ue and feminine suffix la; written accent supplied.
Modelled at pronoun-attachment introduction, then correctly formed without accent after intervening examples; accent supplied.
Correct in Necesitamos leerla without full target model; then contrasted with command léela.
Correct after a negative revisar model, in No revises esta función.

vocabulary.english: don't create (negative tú command of crear)
vocabulary.note: Correct regular-pattern transfer from crear, including crees spelling, in No crees esta función. Not a general lesson on all possible meanings of this written form.
Bare affirmative publica modelled alongside no publiques. Learner subsequently used affirmative object forms; no independent bare publica production.
Introduced c → qu spelling, then correctly used No lo publiques after model.
Valid feminine command after accent supplied, but current target was masculine logo. Meaning mismatch, not a wholly ungrammatical sentence.
Supplied after feminine-object mismatch; immediately retried correctly as publicalo -- es un logo. Written accent supplied.

Correct sequence meaning throughout, but letter transpositions/extra letters observed as priemro, primeor and Primerlo in longer attempts. Standard spelling supplied; no keyboard cause or persistent-language deficit inferred.
Introduced with primero and correctly used in two immediate action sequences; longer-gap recall untested. A later self-chosen sequence used luegoe; corrected to luego. Sequence meaning was retained.
First sequence reverted to probalo. After prueba + lo model, correctly retained ue in focused retry and full sequence. Written accents supplied; delayed recall remains a target.
Introduced as chunk Dime si...; correctly reused in several clauses and a sequence. General decir conjugation or all indirect-object pronouns not taught.

vocabulary.english: whether / if (in an indirect yes/no question)
vocabulary.note: Explained unaccented si in Dime si está lista, distinct from affirmative sí. Correctly used throughout dime-si attempts; full conditional grammar not taught.
Produced correctly in a grammatical sentence with different meaning from requested can publish. Tutor supplied podemos publicar for ability; regular -ar we paradigm not separately taught.
Infinitive introduced with explicar → explica; learner produced command forms, not an independent explicar infinitive sentence.
Correctly used in Explica esta función after regular command model.
Attached me correctly; initial accent absent then misplaced as explicáme. After stress correction, explicitly used correct explícame accent in three consecutive prompts. Longer-gap recall untested.
Introduced as attached me in explica + me → explícame and correctly used. Full object-pronoun paradigm not taught.

grammar.meaning: I want to do something.
grammar.explanation: The verb after quiero stays in its basic form: Quiero revisar esto.
grammar.nextReview: Combine with different familiar verbs without a model.

grammar.meaning: Give a reason using because.
grammar.explanation: Quiero revisar esto porque es importante.
grammar.nextReview: Use a new work-related reason, then revisit after a gap.

grammar.meaning: I want / we want.
grammar.explanation: Quiero is first-person singular; queremos is first-person plural. The plural is not quieremos.
grammar.nextReview: Queremos was recalled correctly in a reason clause and Queremos probarla after intervening material. Longer-term retention remains untested.

grammar.meaning: Negate a statement.
grammar.explanation: No es correcto means It isn't correct.
grammar.nextReview: Correctly placed no between an explicit noun subject and está in La función no está lista; adjective correction was separate. Recheck polarity in a new sentence.

grammar.meaning: Say where someone or something is.
grammar.explanation: Use estar for a person's location: Está en Granada. Ser/estar has other uses that have not yet been taught.
grammar.nextReview: Ask for a short location sentence; supply any new forms needed.

grammar.meaning: I speak / he, she or formal you speaks.
grammar.explanation: Hablo un poco means I speak a little.
grammar.nextReview: Hablo recalled without a hint; full un poco de español phrase needed correction. Revisit the complete phrase after a gap.

grammar.meaning: Spelling encountered during practice.
grammar.explanation: Use ñ in español; porque includes r. Check keyboard constraints before treating accent input as a language difficulty. Affirmative sí has an accent. Autorizado is spelled with z. Posibilidad has one s.
grammar.nextReview: Observe naturally; avoid repetitive spelling drills.

grammar.meaning: You can / you may do something.
grammar.explanation: Puedes + infinitive used for permission and requests: Sí, puedes publicarlo and ¿Puedes revisar esto? In session12 the practised tú form was corrected from podes to puedes, then immediately repeated correctly. Full poder conjugation has not been taught.
grammar.nextReview: Puedes used correctly in three prompted requests after the session12 correction; test unaided recall after a longer gap.

grammar.meaning: Use the first-person form for I authorize.
grammar.explanation: Autorizo is the I form of autorizar. Yo can be stated explicitly. Model: Te autorizo a publicarlo.
grammar.nextReview: Recall autorizo in a natural permission exchange; do not treat a translation question as successful learner production.

grammar.pattern: object pronoun + conjugated verb; infinitive + attached pronoun
grammar.meaning: Introductory object-pronoun placement.
grammar.explanation: Te autorizo places te before a conjugated verb. Publicarlo attaches lo after the infinitive. Reviso el documento illustrates a full noun object after the verb. This is not a complete placement rule; other constructions remain to be taught. With querer + infinitive, both Quiero revisarlo and Lo quiero revisar are possible. If lo follows the infinitive it must attach directly; this is not a blanket rule for all verb combinations. In practised expressions with queremos, necesitamos and podemos, both attached and before-conjugated positions are supported; this does not generalize to every verb combination.
grammar.nextReview: Both attached and before-conjugated-verb positions used successfully in a prompted negative transformation. Test choice of position without instructions after a gap.

grammar.meaning: Ask Why not...?
grammar.explanation: Por qué asks why and uses two words with accented qué. Practised ¿Por qué queremos aprender español? and contrasted it with porque for because.
grammar.nextReview: Question structure correct with a start-phrase reminder; accent and punctuation supplied. Recheck after a gap.

grammar.pattern: object lo versus an unstated subject
grammar.meaning: Distinguish publish it from it is correct.
grammar.explanation: Lo represents the object in publicarlo or revisarlo. In the examples no es correcto and es importante, English subject it is left unstated in Spanish. This does not establish a general rule to omit every subject.
grammar.nextReview: Lo recurred as the subject of readiness in Lo no está listo ya. Recheck unstated subject in readiness versus object lo/la after an infinitive.

grammar.pattern: lo for masculine singular objects; la for feminine singular objects
grammar.meaning: Choose the object pronoun to match a thing's grammatical gender.
grammar.explanation: El documento can be replaced by lo as an object; la función by la. Modelled revisarlo/revisarla, then the learner produced Queremos probarla with la función as the stated referent.
grammar.nextReview: Feminine and masculine command/readiness transfers were correct in this batch. Preserve this evidence without assuming longer-term retention.

grammar.meaning: A little of something; a little Spanish.
grammar.explanation: Use un poco de español for a little Spanish. The learner recalled hablo but omitted de in the noun phrase.
grammar.nextReview: De omitted twice on 10 November, including immediately after a correction. Correct in a cued gap, then Comprendemos un poco de español. Recheck complete chunk without an immediate model.

grammar.meaning: Express purpose: to / in order to.
grammar.explanation: Para comprender = to understand. Compared purpose with a reason clause introduced by porque.
grammar.nextReview: Latest response Necesitamos comprender conversaciones was grammatical but did not express the requested read-to purpose. Leemos para comprender conversaciones modelled; review para + infinitive separately from porque.

grammar.meaning: I read / we read.
grammar.explanation: Leo is the I form; leemos is the we form. Both were supplied, then correctly used in prompted sentences.
grammar.nextReview: Recall forms after a gap and use them in a new sentence.

grammar.meaning: Form the present-tense we form of regular -er verbs.
grammar.explanation: Remove only final -er and retain the stem: leer → leemos, aprender → aprendemos, comprender → comprendemos. Comprender was initially truncated; aprender was then correct after explicit models.
grammar.nextReview: Comprendemos correctly produced twice in this batch, including a next-client-date reply. Recheck aprendemos and other familiar -er forms later.

grammar.meaning: Ask what rather than why.
grammar.explanation: ¿Qué leemos? asks What do we read?; ¿Por qué leemos? asks Why do we read? Word order was correct in practice, while accents and punctuation were supplied; leer was once used for requested aprender.
grammar.nextReview: Ask a new what/why question after a gap and check meaning separately from accent input.

grammar.meaning: We need to do something.
grammar.explanation: Necesitamos leer = We need to read. After a review-it correction, the learner produced Necesitamos publicarlo correctly.
grammar.nextReview: Necesitamos revisarla porque es importante recalled correctly in session12; earlier reviser ending error did not recur. Recheck later.

grammar.meaning: We can / we cannot do something.
grammar.explanation: Podemos leer = We can read. Practised both object-pronoun positions; an affirmative response needed no to match can't before a correct final transfer.
grammar.nextReview: Publicamos was grammatical but did not express requested can publish. After podemos-publicar model, correctly transferred Dime si podemos probarlo. Recheck ability meaning after a gap.

grammar.meaning: It is ready; report readiness with está.
grammar.explanation: Estar readiness chunk está listo/lista has been correctly used and confused with esto in earlier rounds. All four readiness statements in session12 used the right verb and feminine agreement, with accents supplied. Location and a full ser/estar explanation remain separate learning targets.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck readiness and location in separate familiar contexts after a gap.

grammar.pattern: el logo → listo; la función → lista
grammar.meaning: Match this adjective's singular ending to the noun's grammatical gender.
grammar.explanation: Listo with masculine el logo; lista with feminine la función. Initially selected both correctly after models but later mismatched them in a question and negative sentence.
grammar.nextReview: After the session11 feminine error, correctly used lista in four readiness contexts in session12, including two contrast sentences. Recheck after a longer gap.

grammar.pattern: statement word order with yes/no question intonation and ¿...?
grammar.meaning: Ask yes/no questions about readiness or ability.
grammar.explanation: The practised questions can retain statement word order, with questioning intonation and ¿...?: ¿El logo está listo? and ¿Podemos usarla ya? Other word orders are possible. After an explanation, learner produced three structurally correct questions; opening ¿ was supplied.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck a familiar yes/no question after a gap; all current successes were prompted within one practice sequence.

grammar.pattern: todavía no / ya with readiness or ability
grammar.meaning: Not yet versus already/now in the practised contexts.
grammar.explanation: El logo todavía no está listo = The logo isn't ready yet. La función ya está lista = The feature is ready now. Podemos usarla ya and Ya podemos usarla are both natural here; this is not a universal rule for all adverb positions.
grammar.nextReview: Correct not-yet meaning with sentence-final todavía, then valid initial Todavía no... transformation. Recheck after a gap alongside readiness agreement.

grammar.meaning: Connect contrasting statements with but.
grammar.explanation: Pero = but. Learner correctly produced Queremos usarla, pero todavía no está lista and Está lista, pero no queremos publicarla after introduction.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck one contrasting work sentence after intervening material.

grammar.meaning: Standalone this versus this function in the practised request.
grammar.explanation: In the practised general-this targets, esto stands alone: Revisa esto. Before feminine función, use esta función. Learner had correctly used esta función after a model in session13, but esto before función recurred twice during imperative practice; then correctly chose esta in a gap and used standalone esto in a full command. Esta may itself refer to a known feminine item in other contexts; no complete demonstrative paradigm taught.
grammar.nextReview: Correct full Crea esta función after previous corrections, and correct esto throughout test/read requests in this batch. Longer-gap contrast still needs review.

grammar.meaning: Give practical direct instructions using the familiar tú form.
grammar.explanation: Compared ¿Puedes revisar esto? with Revisa esto. Introduced revisar → revisa, crear → crea, leer → lee. These regular affirmative forms were used correctly after models; later crea was recalled, while a read prompt elicited valid formal lea. Demonstratives and spelling assessed separately. Irregular prueba is covered separately; regular negative -ar commands are covered separately; -ir commands have not been taught.
grammar.nextReview: Correct informal lee recalled with tú explicit. Recheck regular command versus infinitive when attaching an object: revisa + la, not revisar + la, for the personal command target.

grammar.meaning: Tell the assistant to test something using the practised informal command.
grammar.explanation: Probar changes o → ue in the affirmative tú command prueba. Learner omitted ue twice after introduction, then correctly selected ue and produced Prueba esto after a model. This example does not teach a full paradigm or all dialect forms.
grammar.nextReview: Probarla infinitive recurred in a longer command sequence; after focused retry, pruébala/pruébalo correctly used in two sequences. Recheck without immediate models.

grammar.meaning: Two valid command forms for informal versus formal singular address.
grammar.explanation: Learner produced grammatical Lea esto por favor during a tú exercise. Tutor acknowledged the formal usted form and supplied informal Lee esto por favor. Only this comparison has been explained; no general formal-command formation rule taught and no intentional register choice established.
grammar.nextReview: Learner correctly used lee with tú explicitly requested; deliberate formal/informal switching remains untested.

grammar.pattern: affirmative tú command + lo/la: revísalo, revísala, pruébala, léela
grammar.meaning: Give a personal command with it as an attached object.
grammar.explanation: For the affirmative commands practised, attach lo/la to the command base and preserve its stress, adding a written accent where needed. Earlier infinitive revisarla needed personal command revísala; subsequent affirmative forms were correctly built, with accents supplied. Negative object placement is covered separately in g-negative-command-objects.
grammar.nextReview: Correct same-sequence contrasts Queremos probarla / Pruébala and Necesitamos leerla / Léela. Written command accents supplied; recheck after a longer gap.

grammar.pattern: regular -ar negative tú commands: no + stem + es
grammar.meaning: Tell the assistant not to do something.
grammar.explanation: Contrasted Revisa esto with No revises esto. Correctly used no revises after a model and transferred the regular -es ending to crear: no crees. Negative object placement is covered separately. Publicar's c → qu spelling is also recorded separately; this is not a full negative-command paradigm.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck negative commands without a model; introduce object-pronoun placement as a separate small unit.

grammar.meaning: Tell someone not to do something to it.
grammar.explanation: Contrasted Revísala and No la revises: affirmative object attached, negative object before the verb. First negative-create attempt creesla needed No la crees. Then correctly used No la revises, No lo revises and No lo publiques. This covers direct-object pronouns practised; other command pronouns not taught.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck positive/negative placement with gender after intervening material; latest publish gender needed an immediate retry.

grammar.meaning: Use publish commands while preserving the stem sound and target object.
grammar.explanation: Introduced publicar → publica and negative no publiques, explaining c → qu before e to preserve the sound. Correctly used no lo publiques. Affirmative publícala was grammatical for feminine but target logo needed masculine publícalo, then correctly retried. Written accents supplied.
grammar.nextReview: Publices omitted qu after intervening material, corrected to publiques; feminine transfer retained qu immediately afterwards. Recheck later.

grammar.meaning: Give two instructions in order: first ..., then ...
grammar.explanation: Introduced Primero revísalo; luego pruébalo. Learner correctly sequenced test then publish twice. First sequence needed prueba stem correction; second retained ue but had a primero letter transposition. Sequencing success is separate from verb-form and spelling corrections.
grammar.nextReview: A self-chosen publish/test sequence retained action order and both command forms. Written accents and luego spelling supplied; revisit after a gap.

grammar.meaning: Ask the assistant to tell you whether something is the case.
grammar.explanation: Introduced Dime si está lista = Tell me whether it's ready. Dime si is practised as a useful command chunk, with unaccented si. Correctly extended to noun readiness, podemos + infinitive, necesitamos + infinitive and a sequence. Publicamos was grammatical but omitted requested ability, so podemos publicar was modelled. General decir conjugation and conditional clauses not taught.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck a practical dime-si instruction after intervening material, preserving requested ability or need meaning and object.

grammar.meaning: Ask for an explanation directed to me.
grammar.explanation: Attached me to affirmative command explica to form explícame, preserving ex-PLÍ-ca-me stress with accent. Learner attached me correctly; initial absent/misplaced accent corrected, then correct explícame accent retained in three prompts. This extends practised affirmative attachment; not a full indirect-object pronoun paradigm.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck explícame after a gap, including stress and practical use.

grammar.meaning: Ask why something is the case using an explanation command.
grammar.explanation: Introduced Explícame por qué... for Explain to me why.... Learner correctly formed readiness, inability and need clauses. Separate words por que were consistently typed, with accented qué supplied. This indirect question has no surrounding question marks in the practised command.
grammar.nextReview: Recheck requested meaning in a practical explanation prompt; supply standard qué spelling without confusing it with clause-formation success.

practiceUnits.title: I want / we want
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We want to review this.
practiceUnits.hint: Start with Queremos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: queremos, without the extra i
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We want to read, immediately after quieremos was corrected.

practiceUnits.title: Say what isn't correct
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: This isn't correct.
practiceUnits.hint: Put no before es.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: no before the conjugated verb
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We don't want to publish it; then move lo before queremos.

practiceUnits.title: Test a software feature
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: I want to test this feature.
practiceUnits.hint: Esta función means this feature; this form has not yet been practised.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: probar used for software testing
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We want to test it; infinitive in command contrast.

practiceUnits.title: Say how much Spanish you speak
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: I speak a little Spanish.
practiceUnits.hint: I speak = hablo.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: hablo for I speak
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: I speak a little Spanish; hablo correct, de omitted.

practiceUnits.title: A goal and a reason
practiceUnits.prompt: Without a model, give a real work goal and a reason using Quiero ... porque ... .
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Quiero revisar esto porque es importante.
practiceUnits.hint: Use familiar words; mixed-language attempts are welcome.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Goal plus reason; the model answer is only one possible response.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: I want to review it because it's important.

practiceUnits.title: Give permission
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: Yes, you may publish it.
practiceUnits.hint: You may = puedes.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: puedes + infinitive; affirmative sí has an accent

practiceUnits.title: Learn a little Spanish
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We want to learn a little Spanish.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Queremos aprender un poco de español.
practiceUnits.hint: A little Spanish = un poco de español.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: queremos + aprender, retaining de; lowercase poco and ñ in español
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Hablo and queremos aprender omitted de; cued gap selected de; comprendemos sentence retained complete chunk.

practiceUnits.title: Purpose or reason?
practiceUnits.prompt: Choose porque or para: Queremos probar la función ___ publicarla.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Queremos probar la función para publicarla.
practiceUnits.hint: Does the gap introduce a purpose or a reason clause?
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: para + infinitive for purpose; porque + clause for a reason
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Requested We read to understand conversations; grammatical need-to-understand alternative supplied.

practiceUnits.title: Keep the whole -er stem
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We understand Spanish.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep comprend-; replace only final -er with -emos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Full comprend- stem correctly recalled in a short-gap sentence; recheck later.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We understand a little Spanish; then We understand Spanish because we read.

practiceUnits.title: Reading in the present
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: I read to get information.
practiceUnits.hint: I read = leo.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Present form leo/leemos with an appropriate purpose or reason.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: I read to get information; then We read because we want to learn Spanish.

practiceUnits.title: Ask what, rather than why
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: What do we read to learn Spanish?
practiceUnits.hint: What = qué; why = por qué.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Match requested meaning, then question structure and standard spelling.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: What do we want to learn?, then What do we read to learn Spanish?

practiceUnits.title: Say what we need to do
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We need to publish it.
practiceUnits.hint: We need = necesitamos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Necesitamos + infinitive; preserve verb ending and requested object.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Explícame por qué necesitamos probarla; infinitive retained.

practiceUnits.title: Can or can't, keeping it
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We can't publish it.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep no for can't and retain the requested object.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Match polarity and meaning; accept both supported pronoun positions.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Requested it answered with grammatical this; then correct publicarla in a transformation.

practiceUnits.title: Ready: listo or lista?
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: The feature isn't ready.
practiceUnits.hint: Match the ending to la función and keep no before está.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Stable está chunk and noun/adjective agreement; assess negation separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Feminine not-yet retry, test reason and two contrasts; agreement correct.

practiceUnits.title: Use it in context
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We can use it because it's ready; it refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Use la for the feminine object.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Keep the object pronoun and readiness adjective matched to the referent.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: We want to use it, but it isn't ready yet; feminine función.

practiceUnits.title: Not yet or ready now?
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: The feature is ready now.
practiceUnits.hint: Ready now uses ya; not yet uses todavía no.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Match time meaning, polarity and noun gender; accept natural ya placement variations.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Can't publish this yet; then initial todavía with feminine publicarla after a model.

practiceUnits.title: Turn a familiar statement into a question
practiceUnits.prompt: Ask: Can we use it now? It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep the familiar word order and use question punctuation.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Question structure and correct object gender; treat supplied accents/punctuation separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Is the logo ready? Can we use it? Can we use it now (feature)?

practiceUnits.title: Connect a contrast with pero
practiceUnits.prompt: Say: We want to use it, but it isn't ready yet. It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: Queremos usarla, pero todavía no está lista.
practiceUnits.hint: But = pero.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Contrast connector, time meaning and consistent feminine reference.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Want to use it but not ready yet; ready but don't want to publish it.

practiceUnits.title: Ask someone to review this
practiceUnits.prompt: Ask: Can you review this?
practiceUnits.hint: Use the familiar tú request form; distinguish standalone this from this function.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Puedes and standalone esto. A grammatical request with different meaning should be acknowledged separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Test this; test this function (grammatical the-function response); review this function.

practiceUnits.title: Tell the assistant what to do
practiceUnits.prompt: Tell the assistant: Review this function, please.
practiceUnits.hint: Regular affirmative tú: revisar → revisa; distinguish general this from this function.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Command verb independently assessed from esto/esta and spelling; do not give the model before a recall attempt.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Read this function, with informal tú explicit.

practiceUnits.title: Tell the assistant to test something
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Test this function, please.
practiceUnits.hint: Probar has the stem change o → ue here.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Retain prueba; assess esta función versus standalone esto separately. Keep hint and model hidden for recall.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Initial sequence used infinitive; focused command retry then feminine and masculine full sequences correct.

practiceUnits.title: Give a command with it
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Review it, please. It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Build from the command revisa, then attach la; keep the original stress.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Personal command base versus infinitive, object gender and attachment; written accents assessed separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Revísala in a longer review/explain sequence, accent supplied.

practiceUnits.title: Give a negative instruction
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Don't create this function, please.
practiceUnits.modelAnswer: No crees esta función, por favor.
practiceUnits.hint: Regular negative -ar commands end in -es.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Negative command ending and noun reference; distinguish immediate model-supported use from transfer.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Don't review this function; then don't create this function.

practiceUnits.title: Keep it before a negative command
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Don't review it, please. It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Use no + la + negative command.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Pronoun before negative command and referent gender; contrast with affirmative attachment.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Review it / don't publish it sequences, masculine then feminine; placement correct.

practiceUnits.title: Publish or don't publish
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Don't publish it, please. It refers to el logo.
practiceUnits.hint: Keep qu before e; match lo to el logo.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Spelling change, polarity, pronoun position and gender; valid alternate meanings acknowledged separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Publices needed qu; immediate feminine transfer no la publiques retained spelling.

practiceUnits.title: Give instructions in order
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: First test it; then publish it. It refers to el logo.
practiceUnits.hint: Use primero, then luego, and retain the prueba stem.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Action order, command morphology and spelling assessed separately; hide model for recall.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Self-chosen publish first, then test sequence; command forms correct, accents and luego spelling supplied.

practiceUnits.title: Ask the assistant to report whether
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Tell me whether we can publish it. It refers to el logo.
practiceUnits.hint: Preserve can with podemos + infinitive.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Indirect yes/no clause, requested ability/need meaning and object retention. Valid different meanings acknowledged separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Initial puedes dime mix, then correct reporting clauses in feminine and masculine sequences.

practiceUnits.title: Ask for an explanation
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Explain this function to me, please.
practiceUnits.hint: Build explica + me, preserving original stress.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Affirmative command, attached me and this reference; accent separate from correct attachment.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Explain this function; then explain this to me.

practiceUnits.title: Ask why with explícame por qué
practiceUnits.prompt: Using tú, say: Explain to me why we need to test it. It refers to la función.
practiceUnits.hint: Use por qué for why and an infinitive after necesitamos.
practiceUnits.feedbackFocus: Meaning, clause formation and command/infinitive distinctions; record supplied accents separately.
practiceUnits.lastAttemptVariant: Not-ready clause, cannot-publish clause, need-test clause, then review/explain sequence.
